text:
maria: heads up — customer AcmeCorp says their outbound firewall is dropping calls from our edge GPUs after a config change earlier today

omar: what exactly is being dropped? any logs?

maria: connection attempts to their internal service (TLS) fail with RST. They shared tcpdump showing our source IPs are in 198.51.100.0/28 and 198.51.100.16/28, but those rotated during the day. They only whitelisted the first block.

jess: ah yes this is the per-tenant NAT pool rotation kicking in. we rotate ~every 6–12h for load balancing unless customer opts into sticky egress.

tyler: quick checklist for them: whitelist both CIDR blocks we advertise + the LB healthcheck VIPs, and allow outbound SNI-based proxy passthrough if they're doing TLS inspect. short version: allow IPs AND hostname when possible.

cust-eng: sending guidance to Acme now. question: can we provide a stable readable list they can paste into firewall rules? they asked for a single CIDR if possible.

omar: we can offer two options depending on plan:
- Hosted customers: provide the two active NAT pools per-region (not a single CIDR) + a short rotation window.
- Dedicated/Reserved: we can enable sticky egress (VIP or static SNAT) for their tenant, then they get non-rotating IPs.

jess: also call out port behavior: our SNAT maintains source ports; if they have aggressive port filtering or deep flow timers, SNAT port exhaustion can happen on very high connection rates. recommend ephemeral port range >= 1024 and longer tcp_close timeouts.

maria: I pasted a small curl-based test they can run from their firewall to validate reachability once they add rules:

```
# from customer fw box
curl -v --resolve api.redwood.example.com:443:198.51.100.5 https://api.redwood.example.com/health
```

omar: if they use an outbound proxy requiring CONNECT, they should allow CONNECT to our SNI (api.redwood.example.com) and preserve the original SNI. TLS-inspecting proxies that rewrite SNI will break certificate pinning with our client cert checks.

tyler: @infra-bot can you dump the current NAT pools for eu-west1 and the recent rotation events? we should include timestamps we rotated so cust-eng can correlate.

infra-bot: rotation-log: eu-west1 poolA 198.51.100.0/28 assigned 2103450000 -> 2103453600 ; poolB 198.51.100.16/28 assigned 2103453601 -> 2103457200

cust-eng: perfect, sending both CIDRs + the note about sticky egress as an option. Also mentioned to allow ports 443/80 and healthcheck ping from 198.51.100.30 (LB vip).

jess: addendum for runbooks: if customer can't change firewall rules, we can route their traffic through a proxy peering (VPN) or enable dedicated egress on their account. Both require a config window and change freeze.

maria: thanks team. I'll follow up with AcmeCorp with exact CIDRs, rotation window, and a link to the dedicated egress request form. cc @cust-eng for tracking. :white_check_mark:
